votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Fostering the Use of Technology to Uphold Regulatory Effectiveness in Supervision Act (H R 8278)
votes.bill_title: Fostering the Use of Technology to Uphold Regulatory Effectiveness in Supervision Act
votes.plain_language: This bill orders federal banking regulators to study whether their technology can supervise firms in real time and whether buying new systems is slowed by procurement rules. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Main Street Act (H R 6955)
votes.plain_language: This bill lessens and otherwise modifies banking regulations, including those regarding institution formation, supervision by federal financial regulators, and bank merger requirements. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Main Street Act (H R 6955)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6955 (Main Street Capital Access Act) lessens and otherwise modifies banking regulations, including those regarding institution formation, supervision by federal financial regulators, and bank merger requirements. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Passage — Protecting Privacy in Purchases Act (H R 1181)
votes.plain_language: This bill prohibits payment card networks from using merchant codes that distinguish firearms retailers from general-merchandise retailers or sporting-goods retailers. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — TRIA Program Reauthorization Act (H R 7128)
votes.plain_language: This bill reauthorizes the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program through 2034. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Financial Exploitation Prevention Act (H R 2478)
votes.plain_language: This bill establishes procedures for delaying the redemption of certain securities if an investment company or agent believes that an older individual or an individual with certain impairments has been financially exploited. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — 25th Anniversary of 9/11 Commemorative Coin Act (H R 1993)
votes.plain_language: This bill directs the Department of the Treasury to mint and issue coins to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks on the United States and the establishment of the National September 11 Memorial and Museum at the World Trade Center. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Community Bank Deposit Access Act (H R 5317)
votes.bill_title: Community Bank Deposit Access Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill changes the treatment of certain types of deposits so they are no longer classified as brokered deposits. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — American Access to Banking Act (H R 4544)
votes.plain_language: This bill requires federal financial regulators to review and streamline the application process for the formation of de novo, or new, depository institutions or credit unions. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Keeping Deposits Local Act (H R 3234)
votes.plain_language: This bill increases the amount insured depository institutions may accept as reciprocal deposits. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
